cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players highlight smooth performance on modest hardware and accessible difficulty options.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game runs well even on low-spec or potato hardware.

citations.review_text:
Best fast paced shooter i have played so far by a long margin.
The weapons, movement tech, enemy and level design, music, it all comes together perfectly. And it can run just fine on potato specs too.

Though i want to say a lot of games get tagged as "boomer shooters" those days, this game has basically NOTHING to do with the old style doom-like games. It is so far gone into the extreme of the movement based shooter side of things that it might as well be labelled as its own different genre

Ah! This game brings eyegasm with PS2 graphics, a machine causing a cocky angel to become a sweet maid is so wholesome. There are funny shit you can do in the sandbox, like stroking to one of the enemies. The parry feels so fucking good that punching a coin feels mandatory. The combo wombo epileptic blood shower whilst breezing through the rain is o la la! The second last layer is simply mind-blogging and a nice benchmark to know how potato is your device.
Don't know why some people compare this funny indie endeavor with the ambitious DOOM, where the man with the cake smites them all with his bakery! Both games are great, but one runs in me, and has butt plug support.
Can't wait for the final update and full level editor + mod support!

Note: My playtime on this is much more because I pirated it before buying. Hakita based as fuck. Turned me into a bisexual boykisser. ♡(ŐωŐ人)
pretty fun great choice for low budget pc
Absolute cinema. Played this on a shitty laptop and it runs great(until layer 8), the movement is awesome, and I generally love the gameplay

great game, amazing modding capability, and you can run it on a potato.

gabriel marry me PLEASEEEEEE

claims.claim: Reviewers note the inclusion of customizable difficulty options and accessibility settings.

citations.review_text:
I am not very good at video games. I have been playing with a controller my whole life. I lack a lot of the fine-motor-function in my wrist and find it difficult to use keyboards.

Ultrakill has all kinds of accessibility options that make it possible for me to play while still having the full, difficult, experience.

of course, if that isn't your thing, you can make it unimaginably more difficult.
really fun, really accessibly difficulty-wise because of how customizable the difficulty is, funny robot game

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: The game provides flexible difficulty customization and gameplay-altering assist options.

claims.claim: The game features customizable difficulty settings and gameplay-altering assist options.

citations.review_text:
I've never been particularly into shooters before, but I really got into this one.

The basics are easy enough to pick up while having some great depth with weapon combos. There's also plenty of room to just use your favourites (there's a meta, but you don't need to know any of that to do well and have fun).

The story is really cool as it contemplates some existential questions about life and violence without getting in the way and shaming you for playing the game.

I also appreciate the amount of accessibility and difficulty options, it's quite rare to see.

For being in early access, there's a lot of content and overall polish that I sometimes forget the game isn't finished yet. That alone is something I can't say for any other early access game, so if you've read this far, play it.

I'm not a shooter guy. I got through (most of) Half-Life 2 because I liked the Portal series so I felt like I had to. Never got very far in Doom. Did not play more than a few rounds of Fortnite even when all my friends wanted me to play it with them. Ultrakill, however, is genuinely addicting.

If you've ever played Vampire Survivors, this game has a similar appeal: Everything is happening all at once and yet somehow you're still winning. Unlike Vampire Survivors though you can't just stop playing once you've found a strategy that works, so sometimes you are not in fact winning. But when you are, you feel SO FUCKING COOL.

I think part of the reason it's so good is that it fixes an issue the genre tends to have by default: Most shooters make you switch between actually fighting enemies and looking for health and ammo pickups. Ultrakill doesn't feature health or ammo pickups; your shooting is only restricted by cooldowns and you can heal by dealing damage to an enemy while you're right next to them.

Another nice thing is that the game can be as easy or as difficult as you want. I played on Normal with no assists and generally didn't go for optional objectives, which felt right for me, but if you want to win each level first try you can play on Harmless and enable various gameplay-altering assist features, and if you want to throw your computer across the room you can go for Brutal and try to P-rank every single level. And of course there are many options in between the way I played and those two extremes.

As of writing this I have completed what currently exists of the main campaign (that is, I beat 8-4) and now i'm going secret-hunting. Maybe some day I'll take on the task of P-ranking everything or beating the game again on a higher difficulty. But it's been really fun so far.

citations.review_text: This is my second favorite game of all time. Just everything about is perfect (except performance in cybergrind and 8th layer)

With all jokes aside. I love this game, I truly do...BUT....these bugs need to be fixed. Game is currently in a state everything seems fine until you realize it is not, enemies clip out of bounds, broken conduction, the lag and fps problems since fraud came out. These issues make it harder for me to recommend the game...but as you can see from my hour, I am gonna give the thumbs up still XD I just love the game okay? even with it's jank. So, I hope you do too. In short, buy the game if you want the cheapest price before it goes out EA and experience the game or wait til 1.0 comes out, choice is yours.
